title: Babel
description: Transpile modern JavaScript and TypeScript with Babel presets, browserslist targets, and polyfills.

data.text: Babel converts syntax the browser may not understand — JSX, TypeScript annotations, optional chaining in older targets — into equivalent code it does. It transforms syntax; it does not type-check or polyfill APIs unless you configure it to.
A **plugin** performs one transformation. A **preset** is an ordered collection of plugins. `@babel/preset-env` reads your browser targets and enables only the transformations those browsers need.

rows: Compiler API used by every integration
Transform syntax based on browserslist targets

data.text: `useBuiltIns: "usage"` injects only the core-js imports your code actually needs, based on the target browsers. Without a polyfill strategy, syntax is down-levelled but missing APIs such as `Array.prototype.at` still fail at runtime.

data.title: TypeScript types are erased, not checked
data.text: `@babel/preset-typescript` strips annotations so the build is fast, but it cannot catch type errors or support features that need type information (such as `const enum` across files under some configs). Run `tsc --noEmit` in CI alongside Babel.

data.title: Transpile a directory and inspect the output
data.code:
npm install -D @babel/core @babel/cli @babel/preset-env @babel/preset-typescript core-js
npx babel src --out-dir dist --extensions ".ts,.tsx"
node dist/index.js

items.question: Babel or SWC?
items.answer: Both transform code; SWC is written in Rust and is typically much faster. Babel remains more configurable and has the broadest plugin ecosystem. Many tools (Next.js, Vite plugins) use SWC by default.

items.question: Does Babel bundle my code?
items.answer: No. Babel transforms files; you still need a bundler such as Webpack, Rollup, or Vite to resolve imports and emit bundles.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: Presets are plugin collections; preset-env targets your browserslist.
Babel transforms syntax and can inject polyfills, but never type-checks.
Run tsc --noEmit separately when the source is TypeScript.
SWC is the faster alternative with a smaller plugin ecosystem.
data.takeaway: The classic trap is assuming Babel type-checks TypeScript — it only erases types.
